item.title: Sonoma Valley Democrats to host Feb. 9 forum for Thompson, primary challengers
item.description: The Sonoma Valley Democrats will host a virtual meeting for the public to hear from U.S. Rep. Mike Thompson, D-St. Helena, and his two Democratic challengers for California's 4th Congressional District seat, Eric Jones and Trevor Merrell.

item.title: Best green coffee bean supplement
item.description: Green coffee beans are just unroasted coffee beans, and they have many of the same benefits you get from a good cup of coffee.

item.title: Best liquid iron supplement
item.description: If you’re considering taking an iron supplement, opt for liquid iron supplements. They are often more pleasant-tasting, easier to absorb and gentle on the body.

item.title: Supervisors OK Sonoma site to expand area mental health, homelessness services
item.description: The Sonoma County Board of Supervisors held its 2026 Goal Setting Session at the Sonoma Veterans Memorial Building on Feb. 3, where city and valley residents spoke about local issues and county officials approved a new mental health and homeless services center in Sonoma.

item.title: Sonoma’s Larson Park to reopen after nearly a year of remodeling
item.description: Larson Park will reopen with four new pickleball courts, three tennis courts and a baseball and soccer field after almost one year of renovations.

item.title: Sonoma City Council zeros in on disaster readiness, climate and housing as top issues for 2026
item.description: Sonoma City Council discussed the agenda for 2026 at the annual Goal Setting Session on Jan. 30, where city leaders considered input from the public while determining Sonoma's top priorities for the year.

item.title: Supervisors award Sonoma Ecology Center $200,000 grant for wildfire prevention
item.description: Sonoma Ecology Center will use the funds to begin large-scale vegetation treatment in the Sonoma Springs area for wildfire preparedness.

item.title: New van at Sonoma Community Tennis will help players compete across North Bay
item.description: The non profit bought a new van in January that would be available to players traveling for competitions around Northern California.

item.title: Hanna Academy’s second annual ‘Claws for a Cause’ raises $165,000
item.description: Hanna Academy serves students from diverse backgrounds, all of whom require specialized instruction and individualized education plans.

item.title: Sebastopol maker of Bachan’s Japanese Barbecue Sauce selling for $400 million
item.description: Justin Gill in six years took a recipe adapted from his grandmother from his garage to a fast-growing brand of Japanese American barbecue sauce now set to be acquired by a billion-dollar retail and foodservice sauces company.
